clue.text: Authority given to winning party and team possibly

indicators.note: 'and team possibly' offers one possible arrangement of those letters

explanation.surface: An election night: the victors claim their authority, with the backing team alongside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And team' reads as part of the political picture, but it is the whole of the letter supply; the long opening phrase is all definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is the authority a government claims from winning an election.

clue.text: Bring before a court a rule in hearing

indicators.note: what we hear rather than what is written

parts.note: reign = rule; say 'a reign' out loud and listen for a word meaning to charge in court

explanation.surface: Someone is hauled before the judges over a rule, at a formal hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' wants to be the court session of the surface; here it only tells you to listen: 'a reign' is said just like ARRAIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign someone is to call them before a court to answer a charge.

clue.text: Onset of duly damp weather requires channel for water

indicators.note: the onset of something is its start, so the first letter

explanation.surface: When wet weather duly arrives, the garden needs somewhere for the water to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Onset of' takes only the D of 'duly'; the rest of the surface's weather is RAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a drain is any pipe or channel built to carry water away.

clue.text: Nominal trade union featuring in corrupt trial

indicators.note: TRIAL is corrupted into a new order

parts.note: TU = trade union, placed after TI

explanation.surface: A union official, in name only, shows up in a rigged court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt trial' reads as a rigged court case, but 'corrupt' only reshuffles the five letters, and the union abbreviation slips in among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Titular means in name only, as a titular head holds the title without the power.

clue.text: Admire some more spectacles

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are taken

parts.note: the answer runs from the end of 'more' into 'spectacles'

explanation.surface: An instruction to gaze at a few more pairs of glasses, or more shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' looks like a quantity of spectacles; it marks the run moRE SPECTacles, spanning two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: to hold someone in high regard.

clue.text: Pass middle of week covering circuits

indicators.note: the central letters of 'week'

parts.note: the two middle letters of wEEk, split around the next piece

explanation.surface: Midweek, a runner gets through the circuits of the track.
explanation.walkthrough: WEEK has two middle letters, and they go one on each side: E + LAPS + E.
explanation.definitionFit: Time elapses when it passes.

clue.text: Line up TV sitcom, maybe

definitions.meaning: to line up events is to schedule them
a sitcom is one kind of broadcast show; 'maybe' marks it as an example

explanation.surface: A channel scheduling its comedy series for the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' shows the sitcom is only an example. PROGRAMME is the British spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Programme is both the verb for scheduling and the noun for a broadcast show.

clue.text: Start to care about opening for group of sisters

indicators.note: the start of 'care' is its first letter

parts.note: on = about, as in a talk on history

explanation.surface: Sisters begin to take an interest in an opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start to care about' reads as one phrase meaning 'begin to mind'; it splits into C and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A convent is a community of nuns, who are called sisters.

clue.text: Tag reinstated wrongly in commercial area

indicators.note: the letters are put back wrongly, in a different order

explanation.surface: A price tag put back on the wrong item in a shopping district.
explanation.walkthrough: A trading estate is a British term for a zone of warehouses, factories and shops, what Americans might call an industrial park.
explanation.definitionFit: A trading estate is an area set aside for commercial and light industrial premises.

clue.text: A limited study in district

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A brief piece of research carried out in one district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limited study' looks like a small survey; it is READ with its end chopped off.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both name a region of a town or country.

clue.text: Spell with a session of golf and time needed to meet deadline

parts.note: a turn = a spell, a stint

explanation.surface: Someone squeezes in a round of golf while still hoping to hit a deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins TURN to the next pieces. 'Spell' is a period of time here, not magic or spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Turnaround is the time taken to complete a job from receiving it.

clue.text: Striking train drivers should pay attention to it

definitions.meaning: an adjective meaning outstanding, as in a notable achievement

definitions.text: train drivers should pay attention to it
definitions.meaning: a railway lamp or arm that tells drivers to stop or go

explanation.surface: Train drivers on strike, and what they ought to be watching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' seems to describe train drivers walking out; it is a separate definition, the adjective in 'a signal achievement'.
explanation.definitionFit: Signal as an adjective means notable or striking.

clue.text: Retired journalist was waiting for fitting?

indicators.note: retiring is drawing back, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: ED = editor, the standard crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A retired newspaperman is waiting to be fitted for a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitting' looks like a tailor's appointment; it is the adjective, meaning appropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the adjective sense: a reward that is earned is fitting, appropriate to what was done.

clue.text: Sweet honeysuckle's latest thing cultivated in garden

indicators.note: the latest thing of 'honeysuckle' is its final letter
cultivating works the letters into a new shape

parts.note: anagram fodder with the E, 9 letters in all

explanation.surface: Sweet-scented honeysuckle, the newest plant grown in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is fodder, not a link: E + IN + GARDEN are all rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet and endearing both describe something charming and lovable.

clue.text: Divert different trainee to be around conservationists

indicators.note: the letters of TRAINEE take a different order

parts.note: anagram of TRAINEE, split as E…TERAIN
NT = National Trust, the British heritage and conservation charity

explanation.surface: A new trainee is sent to work alongside a team of conservationists.
explanation.walkthrough: NT sits inside the rearranged trainee: E + NT + ERTAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Divert here is the sense of amusing, taking someone's mind off things, not rerouting.

clue.text: Metal worker quiet about first signs of metal in truck

indicators.note: the first letter of each word

parts.words: first signs of metal in truck
parts.note: first letters of Metal, In, Truck

explanation.surface: A silent blacksmith spots the first hint of metal in a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: S + MIT + H. 'In' here is one of the words whose first letter is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A smith works metal, as a blacksmith or goldsmith.

clue.text: Origin, reportedly, in room on ship

indicators.note: as reported, spoken, so go by sound

parts.note: birth = origin; its sound is shared with a word for a bunk on a ship

explanation.surface: A rumour about where someone came from, passed round a ship's cabin.
explanation.walkthrough: BIRTH and BERTH sound alike, so 'reportedly' turns the origin into the ship's sleeping place.
explanation.definitionFit: A berth is a sleeping place or cabin on a ship.

clue.text: European obtained parting message in selfish venture

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, the farewell on a gravestone

explanation.surface: A European receives a farewell note during some self-serving scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parting message' sounds like a goodbye card; it is the final parting, the RIP on a headstone.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is an activity undertaken to boost one's own self-importance.

clue.text: Female in neat base prepared celebratory meal

indicators.note: the letters are prepared, made up into a new form

parts.note: anagram of NEAT BASE, split as BEAN…EAST

explanation.surface: A woman in a tidy camp gets a party dinner ready.
explanation.walkthrough: A beanfeast, or beano, is British slang for a jolly party with food. BEAN + F + EAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanfeast was originally an annual dinner for workers, hence a celebratory meal.

clue.text: Note person who has an inherent talent

definitions.meaning: in music, the sign that cancels a sharp or flat, and the note it marks

definitions.text: person who has an inherent talent
definitions.meaning: someone born gifted at a thing, a noun sense

explanation.surface: Take note of the gifted one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like an instruction to pay attention; it is a noun from music, the NATURAL sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural names both a musical note and a person with an innate gift.

clue.text: Use the internet and start to enjoy it in abundance

indicators.note: the start of 'enjoy' is its first letter

explanation.surface: Advice to go online and have fun with it to your heart's content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use the internet' is SURF, as in surfing the web; 'start to' takes only the E of 'enjoy'.
explanation.definitionFit: A surfeit is an excess, more than enough of something.

clue.text: I want to wander around a Pacific Ocean island

indicators.note: the letters wander out of order
the rearranged letters go around A

parts.note: anagram of I WANT, split as T…IWAN

explanation.surface: Someone longing to roam round an island in the Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: The traveller's wish in the surface is the machinery: T + A + IWAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Taiwan is one of many islands in the western Pacific.

clue.text: Rota devised in job to get slowly cooked meat dish

indicators.note: the letters of ROTA are devised afresh

parts.note: a post = a job, split as PO…ST

explanation.surface: A kitchen rota drawn up so the pot roast gets made.
explanation.walkthrough: A rota is a British word for a duty roster. PO + TROA + ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot roast is a joint of meat browned then cooked slowly in a covered pot.

clue.text: That fellow is captivated by Conservative system of ideas

parts.note: Tory = Conservative, the British party, split as T…ORY

explanation.surface: A man falls for a Conservative political ideology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Captivated' suggests charm, but in crosswords being captured means being held inside another word; the fellow is enclosed by the party name.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a system of ideas meant to explain something.

clue.text: Go into US headquarters avoiding cold

parts.note: center, the American spelling, as in a command center

explanation.surface: Entering an American head office while dodging the chill outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US' flags the American spelling CENTER; without C it leaves ENTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to enter a room is to go into it.

clue.text: Poorly rated runners need it and fail to make progress

indicators.note: the letters of 'rated' are in poor order

explanation.surface: Low-ranked athletes need something and can't get ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poorly rated runners' reads as one phrase about weak athletes; 'poorly rated' makes TREAD and 'runners need it' is WATER.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread water is to stay in place without advancing.

clue.text: Recall walker tiring in part in long journey on foot

indicators.note: calling back, so the letters run backwards
only part of the words is used

explanation.surface: Remembering a hiker who began to flag partway through a long hike.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer's own subject, a tiring walker, hides it backwards across the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym; trek comes from Afrikaans for a long hard journey by ox-wagon, now mostly on foot.

clue.text: Old writer in front of gallery for launch

indicators.note: the front of 'gallery' is its first letter

explanation.surface: An elderly author stands before an art gallery at its launch night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In front of' looks like a position; it splits into IN and 'front of', which takes G.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the event: a gallery's opening night is its launch.

clue.text: Revised trail in Cyprus showing intelligible character

indicators.note: the letters of TRAIL are revised into a new order
'in' places the rearranged trail inside Cyprus, between its C and Y

parts.note: CY = Cyprus, its international code, split as C…Y

explanation.surface: A new hiking route on Cyprus shows off a clear-headed local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' sounds like a person; here it means quality, so the definition is the quality of being intelligible.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarity is the quality of being clear and easy to understand.
